commit_message:
[LinalgExt] Add a  output sizes < number of batch dims check in `iree_linalg_ext.im2col` verifier (#24925)

Adds a check to ensure that the number of output sizes is greater than
or equal to the number of batch dims for the `iree_linalg_ext.im2col`
op. Without this, a batch dim index would be out of bounds when
resolving a size from the output sizes array.

`Assisted-by: Claude Code`

Signed-off-by: Ayokunle Amodu <ayokunle321@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Expand im2col test coverage

Cover the layouts, ranks and element types the generic rewrite claims
to handle: channels-last filters (nhwc_fhwc), 1-D ncw, 3-D 3x3x3 in
both channels-first and channels-last layouts, 3-D with unit spatial
window loops, channels-last groups, depthwise with a channel
multiplier, and mixed-precision bf16 -> f32 named convolutions.

Every rewritten case now checks the gather read map and the
contraction indexing maps, not only the shapes. Quantized
convolutions join the existing depthwise and pooling negative cases.

commit_message:
[Compiler][Codegen] expose loop-return allocation control arg

Custom pipelines may return fresh buffers from loops and manage their
lifetime after bufferization. Empty-tensor analysis must honor the same
policy as bufferization so it does not reject otherwise supported IR,
while callers that do not opt in retain the existing equivalence requirement.

Co-authored-by: Luis Romero <115032777+L-roro@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Bubble pads through multi-use dequantizes

BubblePadThroughDequantize required the dequantize to have the pad as
its only user. A dequantized activation that feeds both a padded
convolution and another consumer, such as a residual add or concat,
kept its pad on the real-valued side, so the convolution never saw a
dequantize producer and stayed in floating point.

Moving the pad does not need exclusive ownership: the padded positions
get their own dequantize of the padded quantized value, while the other
users keep reading the original dequantize. Drop the restriction.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>
name: setup / setup

[GlobalOptimization] Bubble pads through multi-use dequantizes

BubblePadThroughDequantize required the dequantize to have the pad as
its only user. A dequantized activation that feeds both a padded
convolution and another consumer, such as a residual add or concat,
kept its pad on the real-valued side, so the convolution never saw a
dequantize producer and stayed in floating point.

Moving the pad does not need exclusive ownership: the padded positions
get their own dequantize of the padded quantized value, while the other
users keep reading the original dequantize. Drop the restriction.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>
name: Test Android / android_arm64

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Bubble pads through multi-use dequantizes

BubblePadThroughDequantize required the dequantize to have the pad as
its only user. A dequantized activation that feeds both a padded
convolution and another consumer, such as a residual add or concat,
kept its pad on the real-valued side, so the convolution never saw a
dequantize producer and stayed in floating point.

Moving the pad does not need exclusive ownership: the padded positions
get their own dequantize of the padded quantized value, while the other
users keep reading the original dequantize. Drop the restriction.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMGPU] Fix hardcoded LHS transpose shape in NV mma.sync lowering (#24676)

This PR is stacked on:
- [x] https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/24659

## Description

`createMmaOp()` hardcoded the LHS reshape shape to `{2, 2, 2}` when
lowering NV `mma.sync`. This held for all NV intrinsics that existed at
the time (F16/BF16 m16n8k16, `element[K]=2`), but FP8 m16n8k32 packs
`element[K]=4`, so the reshape produced 16 elements while the hardcoded
target expected 8:


> error: 'vector.shape_cast' op has different number of elements at
source (16) and result (8)
> note: see current operation: %73 = "vector.shape_cast"(%70) :
(vector<2x1x2x4xf8E4M3FN>) -> vector<2x2x2xf8E4M3FN>

This computes the reshape shape from `getSingleSubgroupLayout()` instead
of hardcoding it, so it adapts to any `element[K]` size. F16/BF16
behavior is unchanged (`{2, 2, 2}` still holds for them).

Adds an FP8 (E4M3FN) TileAndFuse pipeline test.

## Testing

```bash
/workspace/iree-build/tools/iree-opt \
    --split-input-file \
    --iree-codegen-llvmgpu-nvvm-lowering-pipeline="include-llvm-lowering=false" \
    compiler/src/iree/compiler/Codegen/LLVMGPU/test/NVVM/pipeline_tile_and_fuse_mma_sync.mlir \
    | /workspace/iree-build/llvm-project/bin/FileCheck \
      compiler/src/iree/compiler/Codegen/LLVMGPU/test/NVVM/pipeline_tile_and_fuse_mma_sync.mlir

---------

Signed-off-by: weimin023 <tnwilly@gmail.com>
name: linux_x64_gcc

commit_message:
[Torch] Convert PT2E per-channel-group quantization to LinalgExt

Convert the typed PT2E quantize_per_channel_group and
dequantize_per_channel_group ops to iree_linalg_ext.quantize_affine and
dequantize_affine before Torch-to-Linalg expands them, so later QDQ
optimizations keep the group structure instead of floordiv-indexed
arithmetic. LinalgExt indexes parameters with projected permutations, so
the ops work on the input with its last dimension split into groups and
their result is collapsed back; the type of that view is derived from
the group size in one place. A group size beyond the row with one scale
per row is read as a single group spanning the row, as PT2E does.

Ops LinalgExt cannot express remain for the Torch-to-Linalg lowering:
groups that do not evenly split a static last dimension of a rank-2
input, flattened group parameters, bool zero points, which LinalgExt
would sign-extend to -1, non-float real values, and f16 or bf16 scales
on quantize, which would round f32 real values.

Grouped dequantization matches the PT2E reference, including bf16
scales. The per-channel-group reference adds the zero point before
rounding, so exact ties round differently for odd zero points, as they
do in Torch-to-Linalg.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

dequantize_per_channel_group ops to iree_linalg_ext.quantize_affine and
dequantize_affine before Torch-to-Linalg expands them, so later QDQ
optimizations keep the group structure instead of floordiv-indexed
arithmetic. LinalgExt indexes parameters with projected permutations, so
the ops work on the input with its last dimension split into groups and
their result is collapsed back; the type of that view is derived from
the group size in one place. A group size beyond the row with one scale
per row is read as a single group spanning the row, as PT2E does.

Ops LinalgExt cannot express remain for the Torch-to-Linalg lowering:
groups that do not evenly split a static last dimension of a rank-2
input, flattened group parameters, bool zero points, which LinalgExt
would sign-extend to -1, non-float real values, and f16 or bf16 scales
on quantize, which would round f32 real values.

Grouped dequantization matches the PT2E reference, including bf16
scales. The per-channel-group reference adds the zero point before
rounding, so exact ties round differently for odd zero points, as they
do in Torch-to-Linalg.

commit_message:
[LLVMGPU] Fix hardcoded LHS transpose shape in NV mma.sync lowering (#24676)

This PR is stacked on:
- [x] https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/24659

## Description

`createMmaOp()` hardcoded the LHS reshape shape to `{2, 2, 2}` when
lowering NV `mma.sync`. This held for all NV intrinsics that existed at
the time (F16/BF16 m16n8k16, `element[K]=2`), but FP8 m16n8k32 packs
`element[K]=4`, so the reshape produced 16 elements while the hardcoded
target expected 8:


> error: 'vector.shape_cast' op has different number of elements at
source (16) and result (8)
> note: see current operation: %73 = "vector.shape_cast"(%70) :
(vector<2x1x2x4xf8E4M3FN>) -> vector<2x2x2xf8E4M3FN>

This computes the reshape shape from `getSingleSubgroupLayout()` instead
of hardcoding it, so it adapts to any `element[K]` size. F16/BF16
behavior is unchanged (`{2, 2, 2}` still holds for them).

Adds an FP8 (E4M3FN) TileAndFuse pipeline test.

## Testing

```bash
/workspace/iree-build/tools/iree-opt \
    --split-input-file \
    --iree-codegen-llvmgpu-nvvm-lowering-pipeline="include-llvm-lowering=false" \
    compiler/src/iree/compiler/Codegen/LLVMGPU/test/NVVM/pipeline_tile_and_fuse_mma_sync.mlir \
    | /workspace/iree-build/llvm-project/bin/FileCheck \
      compiler/src/iree/compiler/Codegen/LLVMGPU/test/NVVM/pipeline_tile_and_fuse_mma_sync.mlir

---------

Signed-off-by: weimin023 <tnwilly@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMGPU] Fix hardcoded LHS transpose shape in NV mma.sync lowering (#24676)

This PR is stacked on:
- [x] https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/24659

## Description

`createMmaOp()` hardcoded the LHS reshape shape to `{2, 2, 2}` when
lowering NV `mma.sync`. This held for all NV intrinsics that existed at
the time (F16/BF16 m16n8k16, `element[K]=2`), but FP8 m16n8k32 packs
`element[K]=4`, so the reshape produced 16 elements while the hardcoded
target expected 8:


> error: 'vector.shape_cast' op has different number of elements at
source (16) and result (8)
> note: see current operation: %73 = "vector.shape_cast"(%70) :
(vector<2x1x2x4xf8E4M3FN>) -> vector<2x2x2xf8E4M3FN>

This computes the reshape shape from `getSingleSubgroupLayout()` instead
of hardcoding it, so it adapts to any `element[K]` size. F16/BF16
behavior is unchanged (`{2, 2, 2}` still holds for them).

Adds an FP8 (E4M3FN) TileAndFuse pipeline test.

commit_message:
[VectorExt] Reject reshapes that reorder nested layout levels

When merging source dimensions, reshape can consume an element level
after a thread level and change which elements each thread owns.
Track the last level consumed for each target dimension and reject
reshapes that would reorder non-unit levels.

Add tests for forward and backward layout propagation, plus a valid
reshape where each thread's elements remain contiguous.

Fixes #24955

or equal to the number of batch dims for the `iree_linalg_ext.im2col`

commit_message:
[VectorExt] Reject reshapes that reorder nested layout levels

When merging source dimensions, reshape can consume an element level
after a thread level and change which elements each thread owns.
Track the last level consumed for each target dimension and reject
reshapes that would reorder non-unit levels.

Add tests for forward and backward layout propagation, plus a valid
reshape where each thread's elements remain contiguous.

Fixes #24955

commit_message:
[LLVMGPU] Fix hardcoded LHS transpose shape in NV mma.sync lowering (#24676)

This PR is stacked on:
- [x] https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/24659

## Description

`createMmaOp()` hardcoded the LHS reshape shape to `{2, 2, 2}` when
lowering NV `mma.sync`. This held for all NV intrinsics that existed at
the time (F16/BF16 m16n8k16, `element[K]=2`), but FP8 m16n8k32 packs
`element[K]=4`, so the reshape produced 16 elements while the hardcoded
target expected 8:


> error: 'vector.shape_cast' op has different number of elements at
source (16) and result (8)
> note: see current operation: %73 = "vector.shape_cast"(%70) :
(vector<2x1x2x4xf8E4M3FN>) -> vector<2x2x2xf8E4M3FN>

This computes the reshape shape from `getSingleSubgroupLayout()` instead
of hardcoding it, so it adapts to any `element[K]` size. F16/BF16
behavior is unchanged (`{2, 2, 2}` still holds for them).

Adds an FP8 (E4M3FN) TileAndFuse pipeline test.

## Testing

```bash
/workspace/iree-build/tools/iree-opt \
    --split-input-file \
    --iree-codegen-llvmgpu-nvvm-lowering-pipeline="include-llvm-lowering=false" \
    compiler/src/iree/compiler/Codegen/LLVMGPU/test/NVVM/pipeline_tile_and_fuse_mma_sync.mlir \
    | /workspace/iree-build/llvm-project/bin/FileCheck \
      compiler/src/iree/compiler/Codegen/LLVMGPU/test/NVVM/pipeline_tile_and_fuse_mma_sync.mlir

---------

Signed-off-by: weimin023 <tnwilly@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[Torch] Convert PT2E per-channel-group quantization to LinalgExt

Convert the typed PT2E quantize_per_channel_group and
dequantize_per_channel_group ops to iree_linalg_ext.quantize_affine and
dequantize_affine before Torch-to-Linalg expands them, so later QDQ
optimizations keep the group structure instead of floordiv-indexed
arithmetic. LinalgExt indexes parameters with projected permutations, so
the ops work on the input with its last dimension split into groups and
their result is collapsed back; the type of that view is derived from
the group size in one place. A group size beyond the row with one scale
per row is read as a single group spanning the row, as PT2E does.

Ops LinalgExt cannot express remain for the Torch-to-Linalg lowering:
groups that do not evenly split a static last dimension of a rank-2
input, flattened group parameters, bool zero points, which LinalgExt
would sign-extend to -1, non-float real values, and f16 or bf16 scales
on quantize, which would round f32 real values.

Grouped dequantization matches the PT2E reference, including bf16
scales. The per-channel-group reference adds the zero point before
rounding, so exact ties round differently for odd zero points, as they
do in Torch-to-Linalg.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

the ops work on the input with its last dimension split into groups and
their result is collapsed back; the type of that view is derived from
the group size in one place. A group size beyond the row with one scale
per row is read as a single group spanning the row, as PT2E does.

Ops LinalgExt cannot express remain for the Torch-to-Linalg lowering:
groups that do not evenly split a static last dimension of a rank-2
input, flattened group parameters, bool zero points, which LinalgExt
would sign-extend to -1, non-float real values, and f16 or bf16 scales
on quantize, which would round f32 real values.

Grouped dequantization matches the PT2E reference, including bf16
scales. The per-channel-group reference adds the zero point before
rounding, so exact ties round differently for odd zero points, as they
do in Torch-to-Linalg.

commit_message:
[LLVMGPU] Fix hardcoded LHS transpose shape in NV mma.sync lowering (#24676)

This PR is stacked on:
- [x] https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/24659

## Description

`createMmaOp()` hardcoded the LHS reshape shape to `{2, 2, 2}` when
lowering NV `mma.sync`. This held for all NV intrinsics that existed at
the time (F16/BF16 m16n8k16, `element[K]=2`), but FP8 m16n8k32 packs
`element[K]=4`, so the reshape produced 16 elements while the hardcoded
target expected 8:


> error: 'vector.shape_cast' op has different number of elements at
source (16) and result (8)
> note: see current operation: %73 = "vector.shape_cast"(%70) :
(vector<2x1x2x4xf8E4M3FN>) -> vector<2x2x2xf8E4M3FN>

This computes the reshape shape from `getSingleSubgroupLayout()` instead
of hardcoding it, so it adapts to any `element[K]` size. F16/BF16
behavior is unchanged (`{2, 2, 2}` still holds for them).

Adds an FP8 (E4M3FN) TileAndFuse pipeline test.

## Testing

```bash
/workspace/iree-build/tools/iree-opt \
    --split-input-file \
    --iree-codegen-llvmgpu-nvvm-lowering-pipeline="include-llvm-lowering=false" \
    compiler/src/iree/compiler/Codegen/LLVMGPU/test/NVVM/pipeline_tile_and_fuse_mma_sync.mlir \
    | /workspace/iree-build/llvm-project/bin/FileCheck \
      compiler/src/iree/compiler/Codegen/LLVMGPU/test/NVVM/pipeline_tile_and_fuse_mma_sync.mlir

---------

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Bubble pads through multi-use dequantizes

BubblePadThroughDequantize required the dequantize to have the pad as
its only user. A dequantized activation that feeds both a padded
convolution and another consumer, such as a residual add or concat,
kept its pad on the real-valued side, so the convolution never saw a
dequantize producer and stayed in floating point.

Moving the pad does not need exclusive ownership: the padded positions
get their own dequantize of the padded quantized value, while the other
users keep reading the original dequantize. Drop the restriction.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[Compiler][Codegen] expose loop-return allocation control arg

Custom pipelines may return fresh buffers from loops and manage their
lifetime after bufferization. Empty-tensor analysis must honor the same
policy as bufferization so it does not reject otherwise supported IR,
while callers that do not opt in retain the existing equivalence requirement.

Co-authored-by: Luis Romero <115032777+L-roro@users.noreply.github.com>
